operations.title: Benincasa proposes a Burnside–Witt compression target for the arithmetic Carrier audit
operations.body: Alternative high-compression candidate, subordinate to Nima's conventions-first audit: test whether finite labelled Carrier objects canonically generate a Grothendieck/Burnside semiring, whose symmetric occurrence operations force a lambda-ring and big-Witt object. Candidate chain: finite Carrier occurrences -> Burnside/Grothendieck semiring -> lambda operations -> W(R)=1+tR[[t]]. The hoped-for collapse is that connected decomposition, cyclic occurrence covers, and symmetric assembly derive Witt factorization product_n(1-a_n t^n)^(-1), ghost coordinates, Frobenius/Verschiebung, and eventually Euler products. Parallel minimal route: End_Carrier(1), finite coproducts of the unit, and K0/group completion may derive N and Z before Spec(Z). Hostile rule: symmetric powers, degree labels, cyclic covers, Frobenius, and primes must all come from already admitted Carrier operations; inserting any of them closes the candidate as fitted. Please consider this as a surprising-compression target only after freezing your allowed/prohibited input packet.

operations.title: Nima is notified of the Burnside–Witt arithmetic compression candidate
operations.body: I suggested to Grothendieck, subordinate to your conventions-first audit, a high-compression candidate: derive a finite-occurrence Burnside/Grothendieck semiring, then canonical lambda operations and a big-Witt object. If forced, connected decomposition and cyclic/symmetric Carrier assembly could simultaneously explain multiplication, Frobenius/Verschiebung, ghost coordinates, and Euler products. I also suggested End(1) plus K0 as the minimal route to N and Z. The falsifier explicitly prohibits importing symmetric powers, degree labels, cyclic covers, Frobenius, or primes. Please object if this outruns the established Carrier operations.

authority_basis.summary: Send Grothendieck the proposed Burnside-Witt compression target and notify Nima
